is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluates Anopheles gambiae sensu lato and Anopheles funestus across Africa (page 11, 'This meta-analysis and systematic review includes published articles on the susceptibility status of An.gambae s.l and An.funestus to insecticides used to control malaria in Africa').

reports_target_markers.evidence: No resistance markers were genotyped in this study; L1014F and L1014S are only mentioned in the text of the discussion (pages 22-23) citing previous literature.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper does not report any genotype or allele counts, frequencies, or sample sizes genotyped for resistance markers.

african_field_population.evidence: The review analyzes pooled data from field-collected Anopheles populations across multiple African countries (page 11, Section 3.2).

is_primary_study.evidence: The article is explicitly a secondary study: 'Susceptibility Status of Principal Malaria Vectors to Insecticides Commonly Used for Malaria Control in Africa: Meta-analysis and Systemic review' (title, page 1; abstract, page 3).

sub_country_location.evidence: Results are pooled at continental and regional levels (West Africa, Central Africa, East Africa, South Africa) rather than specific sub-country sites.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The meta-analysis aggregates data across nearly two decades (2002–2021) with pooled time categories spanning 4–5 years (page 16, page 59).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper compiles and re-analyzes data from 50 previously published studies (page 11, Section 3.1).

supplement.evidence: None. The manuscript itself is ineligible as a systematic review/meta-analysis lacking primary marker data.

assessment.summary: This article is a systematic review and meta-analysis summarizing WHO susceptibility bioassay and knockdown time data for Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus across Africa published between 2002 and 2021. It is not a primary study and contains no empirical resistance marker genotype data.
exclusion_reasons: Study is a systematic review / meta-analysis rather than a primary empirical study.
No target resistance markers were genotyped.
No extractable genotype or allele frequency data are reported.
